figures.caption: Figure 1. Continual learning with domain preview. Top: CL trains on labeled domains in sequence and is evaluated on all seen domains. Middle: CTTA adapts a trained model to a stream of unlabeled domains and is evaluated on this stream. Bottom: our setup consists of three phases per task, namely training on a labeled domain, preview, where the model adapts online to the unlabeled next domain, and evaluation on all domains seen so far.

Table 1. CL and TTA methods do not combine well out of the box. Accuracy (%) of a ResNet trained with FT (no buffer) or ER (buffer of 200 images), averaged over the six benchmarks of Sec. 6.1, with mixed evaluation batches. No TTA: the CL method alone. +TTA: the naive combination, where the network adapted by a TTA method during the preview predicts every image. Each +TTA and DOSE number is the median over the TTA methods run on each benchmark that keep every core component (up to 18, Supp. Sec. C.1). Old, new: accuracy on the trained and preview domains. Dmg.: latest-domain damage (Sec. 3.3), in points. Forg.: forgetting, the drop of a trained domain between the end of its task and the last task. Oracle: +TTA when each evaluation batch holds a single domain and is normalized with its own statistics (two TTA methods). Trained: the preview domain once trained on with labels.

Figure 2. DOSE. (a) During training, the frozen first block of the initial network gives the recorded statistics of domain t, while a bank stores the BatchNorm statistics of each domain for memory-free CL. (b) TTA adapts online, while DOSE records the statistics of the preview and builds prototypes from the predictions of TTA. (c) For any image, the posterior over the recorded statistics gives λ, which weighs the branch of the preview and the prototypes.

Table 2. Score A (Eq. (1), %) of the CL method alone (no TTA), CL + TTA and DOSE. +TTA and Ours: medians over the TTA implementations that keep every core component of the original method (18 on ResNets and 13 on ViTs, 8 and 6 on C100-C and IN-C, Supp. Sec. C.1, every method and the strict single-pass ones in Supp. Tab. 11). +TTA uses the statistics estimated during the preview, and no method reads the evaluation batch. Bold: best method.

Table 3. Ablations. Score of DOSE, then the difference of each variant to it in points (Tent and ROID, ER and FT averaged, paired by seed). Gray: within 0.5 points. TF/Inet: C100-TF and Inet-TF. Further ablations are reported in Supp. Tab. 20.

Table 4. Setups close to ours. Labeled: data used for supervised training. Unlabeled: data the model adapts to without labels. Labels later: whether these data are labeled afterwards. Evaluation: data on which the reported accuracy is measured. Class-inc.: class-incremental.

Table 5. Optimizers (SGD: momentum 0.9; b = batch size). ImageNet-scale: Imagenette, DomainNet, ImageNet-R/A. The other hyperparameters (margins, thresholds, augmentations: 32 views, 8 on 224-pixel datasets) are the official ones; src/tta/factory.py cites the source of each value. Tent on CIFAR: 10−3, as in the CoTTA code [51], while the PALM benchmark configuration [30] uses 2·10−5.

Table 6. CL learning rate, the CL method alone, seed 0, validation score. Selected: 3·10−5 (ResNet), 10−5 (ViT). Validation accuracies on the CIFAR benchmarks are inflated because the RobustBench ResNet was trained on the CIFAR-100 training images from which the held-out images come.

Table 8. Images per task. Training images are labeled, preview images are not, and the evaluation set of a domain is scored at every later task. ImageNet-R and ImageNet-A (ViT only) also add a corruption at each task. DomainNet caps each class, and some classes have fewer images in some domains.

Table 9. Old domains, preview domain and latest-domain damage, every benchmark (accuracy and points, mixed batches, median over the TTA methods of Tab. 2, per column; “–”: the two protocols coincide on ViTs). +TTA: CL + TTA with its own statistics (batchindependent); +TTAbatch: with the test batch’s (test-batch protocol; on ViTs both coincide). Table 1 averages the ResNet rows.

Table 11. Table 2 over other sets of TTA methods (score, %, medians over the methods of each set, same runs and seeds). Top: every method (9 to 20 per setting). Bottom: strict single pass, without EATA, POEM, DPCore, DAS and ReservoirTTA, which read training or buffer images again during the preview (6 to 14 per setting). Table 2 itself uses the implementations that keep every core component (6 to 18 per setting). Bold: best method.

Table 12. DOSE − CL + TTA for every TTA method, in our batch-independent protocol (score, points; mixed batches; top: ResNets, bottom: ViT-B/16; “–”: not run on this benchmark). Table 2 gives the medians of these columns.

Table 13. DOSE − CL + TTA for every TTA method (score, points; ER, mixed batches; DOSE in the batch-independent protocol, CL + TTA in the test-batch one; “–”: not applicable). For CoTTA, PETAL, RoTTA and ViDA, both systems start each task from the deployed teacher. DOSE is at least as good in 121 of 122 entries.

Table 14. DOSE − CL + TTA for every TTA method, with FT (and ER on C20; score, points; mixed batches; DOSE in the batchindependent protocol, CL + TTA in the test-batch one; “–”: not applicable). Gray: DOSE below the CL method alone. DOSE is at least as good as CL + TTA in 103 of 138 entries and as the CL method alone in 111. Without a buffer on DomainNet, the test-batch protocol gives CL + TTA about 2 points.

Table 15. Seven TTA methods per backbone on the corruption benchmarks (score, points; mixed batches; DOSE in the batchindependent protocol, CL + TTA in the test-batch one; Tent and ROID in Tabs. 9 and 29). Without a buffer on C100-C, CL + TTA with test-batch statistics is 9 to 11 points above DOSE with EATA, SAR and CMF, as for Tent and ROID in Tab. 2.

Table 16. Gain of each TTA method on the preview of a ViT (ER, CL + TTA, mixed batches, 5 seeds): accuracy of the adapted network on the preview stream after the pass minus the accuracy before adaptation, in points; “–”: not run. Bottom: the methods built for ViTs that learn new parameters (prompts, adapters).

Table 17. TTA learning rate ×10: score of CL + TTA/ DOSE (ER, mixed batches). CL + TTA: test-batch protocol, next task from the network it deploys (its teacher for CoTTA), 5 seeds; DOSE: batch-independent protocol, next task from θtr, 5 seeds. DOSE is above CL + TTA in 23 of 25 pairs and at least as good as the CL method alone in 16.

Table 18. TTA learning rate ÷10: same setting as Tab. 17 with the official rate divided by ten, score of CL + TTA/ DOSE (ER, mixed batches, 5 seeds). DOSE is above CL + TTA in 25 of 25 pairs and at least as good as the CL method alone in 25.
Table 19. DOSE without a TTA method (score A, %, 5 seeds): the recorded statistics, the bank and the prototypes on the network that TTA never adapted. No TTA and Ours: as in Tab. 2. Bold: best.
Table 20. Ablations, every cell (score difference to DOSE, points, mixed batches, Tent/ROID, paired by seed).
Table 21. CL + TTA with statistics recorded during TTA instead of those of the evaluation batch (ResNet, mixed): applying the statistics of the preview to every image collapses the old domains.

Table 22. Held-out preview domain: score with the preview domain scored on held-out images never in the stream, and the accuracy of DOSE on the preview domain on the stream and on held-out images. Bold: best of the systems without test-batch statistics; DOSE is best or tied in 23 of 24 settings.

Table 23. Other CL methods (score, mixed batches, Tent/ROID, 5 seeds). Reference: for DER++, the network immediately before each preview within a run of DOSE, which may retain effects of TTA from earlier tasks; for CODA-Prompt, the standalone run without TTA. DER++ alone: an independent run of DER++ that never uses TTA during the whole sequence, within 0.3 points of the reference. +TTA: CL + TTA with its own statistics (batch-independent); +TTAbatch (gray): with the evaluation batch’s statistics (test-batch protocol; on ViTs both coincide).

Figure 3. Preview length (C100-C, ER, DOSE with Tent/ROID, 5 seeds). Solid: accuracy of the adapted network on the preview domain after the pass minus before it. Dashed: score of DOSE minus the score of the same network before the preview.

Table 25. Test-time cost: forward time of the deployed system per image (ms), measured on one RTX A4500 with nothing else running, after the preview of the last task without a buffer, the costliest point of a run (every trained domain has its recorded statistics and a bank entry; domains: number of trained domains). Each row uses the architecture, input size, evaluation batch size (mixed) and number of classes of its benchmark. No TTA: θtr with its stored statistics. +TTA: CL + TTA with the statistics estimated during the preview. DOSE includes the frozen first block, the posterior, the dosed BatchNorm layers and the prototype head. Per-domain BatchNorm with the inferred domain costs the same as DOSE (1.46 and 1.60 times CL + TTA on ResNet-50 and ResNeXt-29). The last two columns give the throughput in images per second (1000 divided by the time per image). Times are measured with the released implementation, separately from the runs.

Table 26. C100-C per task (ResNeXt-29, accuracy, mixed batches, Tent and ROID averaged). +TTA: CL + TTA with the statistics estimated during the preview. +TTAbatch (gray): with the statistics of each test batch, the usual protocol of continual TTA.

Table 27. IN-C per task (ResNet-50, severity 5, accuracy, mixed batches, Tent and ROID averaged). Rows as in Tab. 26. With 1,000 classes, 0.1% is chance. It is a collapse of the predictions, not of the evaluation: at task 2 of the run of seed 0 without memory, one class receives 19% of all predictions of the CL method alone, against 1% at task 0, because the stored statistics of impulse noise do not fit defocused images. Re-estimating the statistics on the same images, as TTA does, brings them back to 28.5%.

Table 28. Cityscapes → ACDC per task (DeepLabV3+ R50, mIoU, 5 seeds). Left: the preview condition. Right: the mean over the trained domains (Cityscapes and the conditions trained so far). +TTA: CL + TTA with the statistics estimated during the preview.

Table 29. Protocols (ResNet, score averaged over the six benchmarks, Tent and ROID). Each row says where the statistics come from and how batches are formed, and both methods get the same statistics. UnMix-TNS runs around ROID. On the same ROID runs, CL + TTA scores 42.9/45.4 (batch-independent) and 54.4/58.0 (test-batch), and DOSE 55.8/61.6 (FT/ER).

Table 32. Balanced score B = 1 2 (old + new) (%, mixed batches, median over the TTA methods of Tab. 2). Old is the mean accuracy on the trained domains and new the accuracy on the preview domain, both averaged over tasks. Columns and systems are those of Tab. 2, and bold marks the best system that uses no statistic of the evaluation batch.

Table 33. Cityscapes → ACDC (score, mIoU %, DeepLabV3+ with a ResNet-50 and SegFormer-B5). +TTA uses the statistics estimated during the preview. Tent is the original method on DeepLabV3+, and on SegFormer, whose only BatchNorm layers are in its head, the version released with the official CoTTA code [51] for this benchmark, which adapts the affine parameters of every normalization layer. DOSE without prototypes (see text). –: not run.

Figure 4. Along the 14-domain streams (ER, Tent, mixed batches). (A) Accuracy on the trained domains after each preview. (B) Online accuracy on the preview domain during its stream. Each preview batch is predicted before the adaptation on that batch: Tent predicts it, normalized with its own statistics, then updates on it. DOSE and CL + TTA share these online predictions, and the CL method alone predicts with its unchanged network.

Figure 5. The domains as seen by the recorded statistics. t-SNE of the vectors s(x) (channel means and log-variances of the input and of the frozen first block) for 300 training images per domain. In parentheses is the domain accuracy of the posterior on held-out images.

Table 34. A preview that is half old images (score A, Tent and ROID, ER and FT, 5 seeds; a ViT has no BatchNorm statistics, so its two CL + TTA protocols coincide). Pure: the protocol of the paper. Half old: each preview also holds as many images of the trained domains. The filter leaves out of the TTA update the images that the recorded statistics of a trained domain explain better than those of the preview.
Table 35. One against three CL epochs per task (score, ER, mixed batches, mean of Tent and ROID, 5 seeds). +TTA: CL + TTA with its own statistics.

Table 36. BatchNorm-aware CL (ResNet, score, mixed batches, mean of Tent and ROID, 5 seeds). BatchNorm: the runs of Tab. 2 with these two TTA methods, which therefore differ from its medians. Cum.: cumulative BatchNorm statistics. CN: Continual Normalization. +TTA: CL + TTA with its own statistics. Bold marks the best system.

Table 37. Compute per preview domain. FLOPs of the forward and backward passes, counted with the FLOP counter of PyTorch on convolutions and matrix products. Time and energy (NVML counter) on one RTX A4500 with nothing else running, measured over 10 steps and scaled to the whole preview. SimCLR uses two views, batches of 256 (C100-C) and 64 (IN-C, to fit in memory) and a projection head 2048-2048-128. DINO uses 2 global and 6 local crops, a teacher forward pass and a head to 65 536 outputs. DOSE adds 6.7 to 7.5% of FLOPs and 5 to 12% of time and energy to TTA during the preview, while the offline methods cost 18 to 416 times as much and keep the preview. Peak memory: 1.8 and 5.8GB for CL + TTA and DOSE, 14.0 and 11.5GB for SimCLR, 6.9 and 9.7GB for DINO (C100-C and IN-C).
